title: Part 2. Devakinandana Dasa, *Vaishnava-vandana
html:
A Bengali vandana (payar) with ragas and refrains: introduction; Gaura, Nityananda, Advaita and their families; the associates at Navadvipa; the sannyasis; the Gosvamis of Vrindavana; associates in Gauda and Orissa; the author's guru Purushottama; Nityananda's associates; conclusion (pp. 21–36 of the 1910 edition; couplets 1–147)

[p. 21]

Raga abhira.

Refrain: Gorachand is my life, Gorachand is my wealth: spreading the net of prema, Gora has caught the whole world.

1Humbly, holding a straw between my teeth,
I make my plea at the feet of the guru and the Vaishnavas.

2How many Vaishnavas [came] with the descent of Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda —
who can tell them all?

3Even the gods cannot comprehend the power of the Vaishnavas —
and who am I? A child of little understanding.

4Great is the longing of my tongue and the desire of my mind —
that is why I wish to compose a Vaishnava-vandana.

5Whatever I say, I say by the grace of the guru and the Vaishnavas;
do not count it an offence of mine if I break the order.1

6I praise Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra Purandara,
whose sons are Vishvarupa and Vishvambhara.

7I shall praise Vishvarupa — blessed is he, blessed! —
Chaitanya's elder brother, named Sri Shankararanya.

8I shall praise Mahaprabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
who descended to purify the fallen — blessed is He, blessed!

9I praise Lakshmi Thakurani and Vishnupriya,
and I extol Gadadhara Pandita Gosani.

10I praise Padmavati-devi and Hadai Pandita,
whose son is Nityananda, wondrous in His deeds.

[p. 22]

11I praise the merciful Thakura Sri Nityananda,
from whom come dancing, singing and joy for all.

12I praise the two Thakuranis — Vasudha and Jahnava,
whose son is Virabhadra, extolled in the world.2

13With attention I shall praise Sri Virabhadra Gosani,
by whose conduct the whole world is won.

Raga bhatiyali.

Refrain: Gora Gosani is the descent that purifies the fallen. Blessed is Gora's descent, the crown-jewel of sannyasis: so beautiful a name is heard nowhere else.

14With attention I praise first of all Madhavendra Puri —
the first descent on the path of devotion to Vishnu.3

15I praise Acharya Gosani — Advaita, the Lord,
who brought Mahaprabhu into the world.

16With all my heart I praise Sita Thakurani,
I praise her sons — Achyutananda and the others.4

16a(Pundarika Vidyanidhi, the crest-jewel of devotees:
uttering his name, the Lord Himself wept.5)

17I shall praise Sri Srinivasa Thakura Pandita,
renowned throughout the world as Narada.6

18With devotion I shall praise Malini Thakurani,
whom Gauranga with His own mouth called mother.

19With attention I shall praise Sri Narayani-devi,
whom the Lord Himself called "alabati".7

[p. 23]

20I praise Haridasa Thakura, foremost among renunciants:
he gave children treats to make them say the name of Hari.8

21I praise Gopinatha Thakura, renowned in the world,
counted as Brahma for his praise of the Lord.9

22I shall praise Murari Gupta, mighty in devotion,
who in a former descent was called Hanuman.

23I praise Sri Chandrashekhara, cool as the moon;
I praise Acharyaratna, whose fame is spotless.10

24I praise Govinda and Garuda, whose greatness is boundless,
whose right is devotion to Gaura's feet.11

25I shall praise the ambashtha12 named Sri Mukunda Datta,
whose singing surpassed the gandharvas.

26With deep and pure feeling I praise Vasudeva Datta,
whom the Lord kept near Him in Utkala.13

27I praise Damodara Pandita, most dispassionate,
I praise Pitambara, his elder brother.

28I praise Sri Jagannatha, Shankara and Narayana:
great renunciants are these five brothers.14

29I praise the great soul Nilambara Chakravarti,
who promptly foretold the Lord's future.15

30I praise Sri Rama Pandita and Gupta Narayana;
I praise the teachers — Vishnu, Gangadasa and Sudarshana.16

31I praise Sadashiva, and Shrigarbha, and Shrinidhi,
I praise Buddhimanta Khan and Vidyanidhi.

[p. 24]

32I shall praise the brahmachari Shuklambara,
to whom the Lord granted the boon of His own prema-bhakti.17

33I praise Nandana Acharya and Vijaya the scribe,
I praise the great soul Ramadasa Kavichandra.18

34I praise Shridhara Pandita, called Kholaveca,
with whom the Lord was ever in playful quarrel.19

35I praise the beggar Vanamali together with his son:
he unexpectedly beheld the Lord's manifestation.20

36I praise, with respect, Halayudha Thakura,
I shall extol Sri Vasudeva Bhadra.21

37I shall praise Ishana Dasa with joined palms —
Shachi Thakurani loved him dearly.22

38I praise Jagadisha and Shriman, Sanjaya,
with humility I praise Garuda and Kashishvara.23

39I shall extol Gangadasa and Krishnananda,
with joy I praise Sri Rama and Mukunda.24

40I praise Vallabha Acharya, known to all the world,
whose daughter is Sri Lakshmi Thakurani Herself.

41With joy I praise Sanatana Mishra,
whose blessed daughter is Vishnupriya Thakurani.

42I praise Acharya Vanamali and the brahmana Kashinatha,
by whose efforts Mahaprabhu's marriage was arranged.25

42a(All who were at the Lord's wedding festival —
to the lotus feet of them all I bow unceasingly.26)

[p. 25]

Raga suhai.

Refrain: A beautiful descent is the descent of Sri Gauranga: such an ocean of mercy there is nowhere else.

43With attention I praise Gosani Ishvara Puri,
from whom the Lord, teaching the world, took initiation.

44I praise Keshava Bharati — the sage Sandipani:
the Lord Himself made him His guru.27

45I shall praise the feet of Sri Ramachandra Puri:
the Lord said of him that he belonged to Sri Rama's host.28

46I praise Paramananda Puri — in nature Uddhava,
I praise Damodara Puri — in the mood of Satyabhama.29

47I praise Narasimha Tirtha and Sukhananda Puri,
I praise Sri Govinda Puri and Brahmananda Puri.

48I praise Nrisimha Puri and Satyananda Bharati,
I shall praise Garuda Avadhuta, great of mind.

49With care I praise Vishnu Puri Gosani,
compiler of the Vishnu-bhakti-ratnavali.30

50With great devotion I praise Brahmananda Svarupa,
I praise Krishnananda Puri and Sri Raghava Puri.

51I praise Vishveshvarananda, known to all,
whose faith in Mahaprabhu's feet is especially firm.

52I praise Sri Keshava Puri and Anubhavananda […].31

[p. 26]

53I praise the two great souls — Rupa and Sanatana,
who established [the holy places of] the land of Vrindavana.32

54I praise Sri Jiva Gosani, accepted by all,
who, establishing the siddhanta, preserved the foundations of bhakti.33

55I praise Raghunatha Dasa, who dwells at Radha-kunda,
I praise Raghava Gosani, who sports at Govardhana.34

56I shall praise Gopala Bhatta in Vrindavana:
he abides ever together with Sanatana and Rupa.

57With a concentrated mind I shall praise Raghunatha Bhatta Gosani,
the teacher of the Sri Bhagavata in Vrindavana.

58I praise Lokanatha Thakura and Bhugarbha Thakura,
abundant in mercy to deliver souls.35

59With one heart I praise Kashishvara Gosani,
especially renowned in the Mathura-mandala.36

60I praise Shuddha Sarasvati, purest in form,
whose devotion to the Lord's feet is spotless.

61With care I praise Prabodhananda Gosani,
who described the qualities of Mahaprabhu.37

62I praise Jagadananda Pandita — Sarasvati herself,
for whom Mahaprabhu had the highest love.38

63I praise the great soul, Pandita Raghava,
whose glory is manifest in the village of Panihati.

64I praise Purandara Pandita — in valour Angada:
a brahmana saw his tail in his house.39

[p. 27]

65I praise Kashi Mishra, in whose abode [lived] the Lord;
with attention I shall praise Vaninatha Pattanayaka.

66I praise Sri Pradyumna Mishra and Raya Bhavananda,
I praise Kalanidhi, Sudhanidhi and Gopinatha.40

67I praise Raya Ramananda, of great spiritual standing,
whom the Lord esteemed as the rarest treasure of knowledge.41

68I praise Vakreshvara Pandita with his divine body:
within — the splendour of Krishna, without — golden Gauranga.42

69I shall praise Sugriva Mishra — Sri Govinda:
for the Lord's sake he [built] a bridge in his mind.43

70With reverence I shall praise Gadadhara Dasa too,
whose greatness is especially manifest in Vrindavana.44

71With one heart I praise Sadashiva Kaviraja:
ceaselessly mad with prema, he is unaware of the outer world.

72I praise Shivananda Sena, whose body is prema,
whose caste, life and wealth are Gora's two feet.

73Chaitanya Dasa, Ramadasa and Karnapura —
the three sons of Shivananda I shall praise abundantly.45

74I shall praise Mukunda Dasa, pure of heart through bhava:
seeing a peacock feather, he lost consciousness.46

75I praise Narahari Dasa — the abode of prema,
in whose heart Gauranga sports unceasingly.

76I praise Sri Raghunandana, saintly in character,
whose form and nature enchant the world.

[p. 28]

77I praise Raghunatha Dasa, full of the nectar of prema,
by whose character all people are won.47

78I praise Acharya Purandara and Pandita Devananda,
I praise Sri Acharyachandra, full of prema for Gaura.48

79I praise Krishnadasa Thakura of Akaihat,49
I praise Paramananda Puri — the Lord's fellow student.50

80With attention I shall praise Sri Govinda Ghosha,
whose name the Lord Himself made true.

81I shall praise Madhava Ghosha — the object of the Lord's love,
to whom the Lord granted a voice that never breaks.51

82With attention I shall praise Sri Vasudeva Ghosha,
whose songs about Gaura have no end.52

83With respect I shall praise Thakura Sri Abhirama:
a log for sixteen bearers he holds as a flute.53

84With great hope I shall praise Sundarananda Thakura:
he made kadamba flowers bloom on a lemon tree.54

85With attention I shall praise Parameshvara Dasa Thakura:
at the place of sankirtana he made the jackals chant the name.55

86With respect I shall praise Vamshivadana Thakura:
Gadadhara Dasa made [him] a descent of the flute.56

87I praise my chosen master named Sri Purushottama57 —
who can describe his incomparable qualities?

88Even one who has no good qualities he shows mercy to
by the power of his natural compassion.

[p. 29]

89In his seventh year he had the madness of love for Krishna;
his dancing enchants the world, his power is unfathomable.

90Seizing Gauridasa the kirtaniya by the hair,
he imparted his own power and made him sing the praise of Nityananda.58

91Gadadhara Dasa and Sri Govinda Ghosha [are witnesses]:
at his manifestation the Lord found joy.59

92Abhisheka with a hundred and eight pitchers of Ganga water;
omniscience from his very childhood.60

93The karavi flower that was in his ear
before the whole assembly came to smell like a lotus.61

94Through his name all Vaishnavas attain perfection;
his body is the happiness of prema embodied.

95With great devotion I praise Kaliya Krishnadasa,
in divine sacred thread and garments, bearing the splendour of Krishna.62

96I praise Kamalakara Pippalai, sporting in bhava,
who said to the Lord: "Take the stick, give me the flute."63

97I praise Ratnakara's son named Purushottama,
who lives in Nadia, an abode of divine splendour.64

98With attention I praise Uddharana Datta:
together with Nityananda he went round all the holy places.65

99I praise Gauridasa Pandita, who carried out the Lord's will:
he took Acharya Gosani to Utkala.66

100I praise Purushottama Pandita, sporting [in bhava], wise:
the Lord gave him the place of Acharya Gosani.67

[p. 30]

101With one heart I shall praise Saranga Dasa,
I praise Makaradhvaja Kara, the Lord's singer.68

Raga barari.

Refrain: Gora Gosani is the descent that purifies the fallen: by Your mercy all souls are delivered.

102I praise Kaviraja Mishra, Bhagavatacharya,
I praise Sri Madhu Pandita and Ananta Acharya.69

103I praise Govinda Acharya, endowed with every virtue,
who composed the wondrous dhamali of Radha and Krishna.70

104I praise Sarvabhauma — in character Brihaspati:
at the Lord's manifestation a wondrous poetic gift opened in him.71

105I praise Prataparudra Raya, in fame equal to Indra:
the Lord revealed to him the six-armed form.72

106I praise the brahmana Yadunatha and Vipradasa the Oriya,
I praise the brahmana Haridasa and the vaidya Vishnudasa,

107at whose songs the Lord rejoiced especially;
I praise his brother — Sri Vanamali Dasa.73

108Disguising himself, he entered into the play of the gopis;
there is no describing how his prema showed itself.

109I praise Kanai Khutiya, known to all the world,
whose two sons are Jagannatha and Balarama.74

110I praise the great soul, Balarama Dasa the Oriya,
to whom Jagannatha and Balarama are subject.

[p. 31]

111I praise Jagannatha Dasa, master of music,
by the rasa of whose singing Jagannatha is enchanted.75

112I shall praise Shivananda Pandita and Kashishvara,
I shall praise Chandaneshvara and Simheshvara.

113I shall praise Subuddhi Mishra and Sri Shrinatha Mishra,
I praise Tulasi Mishra and Kashinatha Mahiti.

114I praise Sri Hari Bhatta and Balarama Mahiti,
I praise the Pattanayaka named Madhava, the steadfast.76

115With care I shall praise Ramananda of the Vasu line:
in his family they know none but Gaura.77

116I shall praise the brahmachari named Sri Purushottama,
with great devotion I praise Sri Madhu Pandita.

117I praise Shrikara Pandita and the brahmana Ramachandra,
I praise Yadu Kavichandra, full of every happiness.78

118I praise the renunciant Pandita Dhananjaya, sporting [in bhava]:
giving everything to the Lord, he took a pot in his hand.79

119I praise Jagannatha Pandita and Acharya Lakshmana,
I praise Krishnadasa Pandita, purest of heart.

120I praise Suryadasa Pandita, known to the world:
his two daughters are Vasudha and Jahnava.

121With attention I praise Murari Chaitanya Dasa,
whose wondrous deeds are like those of Prahlada.80

122I praise Paramananda Gupta, Jagannatha Sena,
Kavichandra, Mukunda, and with them the boy Rama.81

[p. 32]

123I praise Sri Kamsari Sena, Sri Vallabha Sena,82
I praise Bhaskara Thakura, [in whom is] the greatness of Vishvakarma.

124I praise the maker of songs Sri Balarama Dasa,
whose faith in Nityananda-chandra is beyond words.

125I praise Mahesha Pandita, a great madman [of love],
I praise Jagadisha Pandita, the lover of dance.

126I praise Vrindavana Dasa, the son of Narayani,
who brought to light the Chaitanya-mangala.83

127I shall praise Thakura Krishnadasa of Badagachhi,
whose faith is in Nityananda, in the bliss of prema.84

128With one heart I praise Paramananda Avadhuta:
ceaselessly mad, he is unaware of the outer world.

129I shall praise Anadi Gangadasa Pandita,
I praise Yadunatha Dasa, sweet in character.

130I praise Purushottama Puri and Jagannatha Tirtha,
I praise Sri Rama Tirtha and Raghunatha Puri.85

131I praise Vasudeva Tirtha and Upendra Ashrama,
I shall praise Ananta Puri and Hariharananda.

132I praise Mukunda Kaviraja, spotless in character,
I shall praise the blissful Sri Jiva Pandita.

133I shall extol the one called Shishu Krishnadasa:
nurtured by the Lord, he is an abode of divine splendour.86

134I praise Madhava Acharya, cool with poetry,
whose composed song is the Sri Krishna-mangala.

[p. 35]

135Krishnadasa, the younger brother of Gauridasa Pandita,
I shall praise, and Nrisimha, and Sri Chaitanya Dasa.87

136(With faith I praise Raghunatha Bhatta,
I praise Sri Ramachandra Dasa of the divine eyes.88)

137I praise Sri Shankara Ghosha, of a poor man's ways,
who by playing the dampha won the Lord's love.89

138In supreme joy I praise Acharya Madhava:
as the fruit of devotion he became the husband of Ganga-devi.90

139I praise Narayana Paidari and Shivananda Chakravarti91 —
there is no end to praising the Vaishnavas!

140How many Vaishnavas there are in this descent — beyond counting:
their endless glory cannot be told.

141Endless are the Vaishnavas, endless their glory:
there is no one who could measure it.

142Have I wit enough to praise them?
Even the gods cannot express the purity of the Vaishnavas.

143The teacher of all is the Vaishnava Thakura;
he is far beyond hearing, sight, mind and speech.92

144I take refuge at the feet of the guru and the Vaishnavas:
briefly I have said something in this Vaishnava-vandana.

145Whoever reads and hears the Vaishnava-vandana,
the filth in his heart is removed and his mind becomes pure.

146Whoever, rising at dawn, reads the Vaishnava-vandana
will never know any torment.

[p. 36]

147He will gain that prema-bhakti which even the gods find hard to attain —
with this longing speaks Devakinandana Dasa.

Thus ends the Vaishnava-vandana composed by Sri Devakinandana Dasa.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Cf. the apology for the order in Jiva's vandana (Part 1, v. 6) and in GGD 212.
  2. Here, unlike Jiva's vandana (Part 1, vv. 22–23), Virabhadra (Virachandra) is called the son of Vasudha and Jahnava, i.e. of Nityananda.
  3. Madhavendra Puri is "the first sprout of the tree of prema" (CC Adi 9); GGD 22–25.
  4. According to the manuscripts of 1654 and 1702 (Majumdar) this reads "I praise her son Sri Achyutananda": these manuscripts name no other son of Advaita; cf. Part 1, vv. 33–35.
  5. The editor puts this couplet in brackets (apparently it is not in all manuscripts). GGD 54–56: Pundarika Vidyanidhi is Vrishabhanu; the Lord called him "father" and wept remembering him (CB Madhya 7).
  6. GGD 90.
  7. The meaning of the word "alabati" (ālabāṭī) here is unclear; it may be connected with Narayani's receiving the remnants of the Lord's meal (cf. Part 1, v. 36).
  8. GGD 93–95 (Brahma and Prahlada).
  9. Apparently Gopinatha Acharya (GGD 75 — Brahma); see Part 1, note to v. 39.
  10. See Part 1, note to v. 40: Acharyaratna is according to the CC a title of Chandrashekhara, but the vandanas and GGD 103 name him separately.
  11. GGD 116–117.
  12. Ambashtha — the caste of vaidyas (physicians).
  13. On Vasudeva Datta in Puri — CC Madhya 11, 15. GGD 140 (the singer Madhuvrata).
  14. Cf. Part 1, v. 43 and note.
  15. GGD 104 (Garga).
  16. On "Gupta Narayana" see Part 1, note to v. 45. Nimai's teachers — Part 1, v. 46.
  17. CB Madhya: the Lord ate rice from the beggar's bag of the brahmachari Shuklambara; GGD 191.
  18. Cf. Part 1, vv. 48–49: in Jiva, in place of Nandana Acharya, there is Ratneshvara Acharya, and Ramadasa and Kavichandra are apparently two persons.
  19. CB Adi-khanda — Nimai's playful quarrels with Shridhara about the price of banana leaves and about his poverty; GGD 133.
  20. Cf. Part 1, v. 49 and note (GGD 114).
  21. GGD 134 (Halayudha). "Vasudeva Bhadra" — cf. Vaishnavabhidhana (Part 3, v. 17).
  22. Ishana, the servant in the Lord's household, who served Shachi and Vishnupriya.
  23. Cf. Part 1, vv. 51–52.
  24. Cf. Part 1, v. 52 and note.
  25. GGD 49–50; cf. Part 1, v. 55.
  26. The editor puts this couplet in brackets; Majumdar does not count it.
  27. GGD 52: Keshava Bharati is the sage Sandipani, Krishna's guru.
  28. Cf. GGD 92 and Part 1, note to v. 58.
  29. GGD 118 (Paramananda Puri — Uddhava); on Damodara Puri — Part 1, note to v. 59.
  30. Vishnu Puri's Bhakti-ratnavali; see Part 1, v. 61.
  31. The second line of the couplet is missing in the edition (a blank space in the scan). Cf. Part 1, v. 63: "Anubhavananda and Chidananda".
  32. Rupa and Sanatana uncovered the lost holy places of Vrindavana at the Lord's command (CC Madhya 23 and elsewhere).
  33. In Jiva's vandana Jiva himself is naturally not praised; here his name is present.
  34. Cf. Part 1, vv. 70–71 and notes.
  35. At this point Devakinandana's "great" vandana (according to Majumdar) adds Vaishnavas of other sampradayas (Vishnusvami, Hit Harivamsha, Surdas and others).
  36. Kashishvara Gosvami (GGD 166), who served the Deity of Govinda in Vrindavana.
  37. In the Sri Chaitanya-chandramrita (`../chaitanya-chandramrita/`); GGD 163.
  38. According to GGD 51 Jagadananda is a manifestation of Satyabhama; "Sarasvati" — so also in Jiva (Part 1, v. 38).
  39. GGD 91 (Angada); Part 1, v. 76.
  40. According to Majumdar this couplet is not in the old manuscripts: the names Kalanidhi and Sudhanidhi (brothers of Ramananda Raya) occur only in the CC (Madhya 10), and the couplet was apparently added from it. Pradyumna Mishra — CC Antya 5; Bhavananda Raya, Ramananda's father (GGD 122); Gopinatha is Gopinatha Pattanayaka, Ramananda's brother (CC Antya 9).
  41. CC Madhya 8; GGD 120–124.
  42. I.e. in Vakreshvara both Krishna and Gaura are manifest. GGD 71–73.
  43. See Part 1, vv. 81–82 and 111 and notes.
  44. Cf. Part 1, v. 83; GGD 154–155.
  45. Shivananda Sena and his sons Chaitanya Dasa, Ramadasa and Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda Dasa), the author of GGD (GGD 4, 145). According to Majumdar this couplet is not in the old manuscripts.
  46. CC Madhya 15; Part 1, vv. 87–88.
  47. Probably the same Raghunatha (the vaidya) as in Part 1, v. 91.
  48. Acharyachandra — cf. Vaishnavabhidhana (Part 3, v. 29). At this place Jiva has Acharyaratna (Part 1, v. 93; Majumdar notes this too).
  49. Krishnadasa of Akaihat, an associate of Nityananda (named in the lists of the branches of the tree of devotion, CC Adi).
  50. Cf. Part 1, v. 92 (Paramananda Pandita).
  51. The Ghosha brothers, kirtana singers (GGD 188). "A voice that never breaks" is the Lord's gift to Madhava Ghosha's singing.
  52. Vasudeva Ghosha's padas about Gaura — see `../padas/`.
  53. GGD 126: "a log that only thirty-two men could lift"; Jiva (Part 1, v. 95) — "many".
  54. CB Antya 5 describes this miracle in Raghava's house at Panihati as performed by Nityananda; so too Jiva (Part 1, v. 75).
  55. GGD 132; Part 1, v. 99.
  56. I.e., apparently, Gadadhara Dasa revealed that Vamshivadana is the incarnation of Krishna's flute (GGD 179). The line is unclear.
  57. Purushottama Dasa (Nagara Purushottama), son of Sadashiva Kaviraja (CC Adi 11; GGD 131), Devakinandana's guru; cf. Part 1, v. 94. According to Majumdar Devakinandana was his disciple (so also Manohara Dasa in the Anuraga-valli, 1696), so the vandana dates from the sixteenth century.
  58. Gauridasa the kirtaniya is not Gauridasa Pandita of Ambika (v. 99). The story is known only from this vandana.
  59. The line is unclear: perhaps Gadadhara Dasa and Govinda Ghosha are named as those in whose presence Purushottama's greatness was revealed.
  60. I.e. abhisheka was performed for him with a hundred and eight pitchers of Ganga water, and from childhood he was omniscient.
  61. Cf. Part 1, v. 94.
  62. Kala Krishnadasa — GGD 132; Part 1, v. 101.
  63. GGD 128 (Mahabala); Part 1, v. 100. The request "give me the flute" is in the mood of a cowherd friend.
  64. Cf. Part 1, v. 101 and note: Jiva has "Purushottama Tirtha" at this place.
  65. GGD 129; Part 1, v. 134.
  66. Cf. Part 1, v. 97 and note.
  67. The line is unclear. Purushottama Pandita is a singer in the Lord's kirtana.
  68. Saranga (Sharnga) Thakura — GGD 172, Part 1, v. 102; Makaradhvaja — GGD 141, Part 1, v. 103.
  69. Cf. Part 1, vv. 104–105 and notes.
  70. Dhamali — playful songs about Radha and Krishna. GGD 41: Govinda Acharya is Paurnamasi.
  71. GGD 119; on Sarvabhauma's verses about the Lord (the Chaitanya-shataka) — CC Madhya 6.
  72. According to CC Madhya 6 the six-armed form was shown to Sarvabhauma; the vandanas say this of Prataparudra (cf. Part 1, v. 106).
  73. Cf. Part 1, vv. 107–108.
  74. CC Madhya 15 (Kanai Khutiya as Nanda at the Nandotsava festival); Part 1, vv. 109–110.
  75. Cf. Part 1, v. 110 and note.
  76. Oriya associates in Puri; cf. Part 1, vv. 112–114.
  77. Ramananda Vasu of Kulinagrama (GGD 173).
  78. Cf. Part 1, v. 117 (Jiva has Shridhara Pandita).
  79. Cf. Part 1, v. 118.
  80. CC Adi 11; Part 1, v. 120.
  81. Cf. Part 1, v. 121; Vaishnavabhidhana (Part 3, v. 44): "Kavichandra, Sri Mukunda, Sri Rama".
  82. At this place Jiva has "Sri Vallabhacharya" (Part 1, v. 122 and note).
  83. Chaitanya-mangala — the original title of Vrindavana Dasa's Chaitanya-bhagavata.
  84. Cf. the account in Jiva's vandana of Krishnadasa's separation from Nityananda (Part 1, vv. 125–128).
  85. Sannyasis — cf. GGD 97, 100–101 and Part 1, vv. 130–131.
